newsDocuments.headline: Oil slips from near six-months highs despite supply concerns

segments.text: BEIJING: Oil prices fell on Monday ​after surging to near six-month highs ‌late last week, although ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in ​focus.
US crude futures were down $1.60, ​or 1.55%, at $101.67 per barrel by ⁠0018 GMT.
Brent crude futures ​were down $1.56 or 1.34% at $115.16.

newsDocuments.headline: Oil price hike poses challenges for Fed policymakers

segments.text: Additionally, a late spike in Brent crude oil prices, which briefly exceeded $117 per barrel, settled at approximately $116.75 by Friday’s close.
Two main factors contributing to this situation are geopolitical uncertainties and increasing oil prices, which hinder economic activity, and escalate the inflationary pressures.
Conversely, the rise in oil prices is contributing to inflationary pressures, which, in turn, is affecting Treasury yields.
